summary: PulseGuard v0.6.24 hardens the WinGet update stage and improves post-fix reporting so application updates, Windows-component crashes, Store package state, Defender state, and optimization history are represented accurately.

sections.heading: WinGet stays visible, then closes automatically
sections.detail: FIX + OPTIMIZE ALL opens an elevated visible Command Prompt and runs winget upgrade --all. If updates take several minutes, the window stays open for the entire update process. After WinGet actually finishes, PulseGuard keeps the final result visible for 5 seconds and then closes CMD automatically.

sections.heading: WinGet is now auditable in the full report
sections.detail: PulseGuard streams WinGet output live while also capturing the command, elevation state, start/finish time, duration, exit code, detected upgrade count when WinGet exposes one, status, log path, and complete captured output in the consolidated report.

sections.heading: Optimization history survives the automatic post-fix rescan
sections.detail: The automatic Full Health Rescan no longer clears OptimizationSteps or OptimizationChanges. The latest repair workflow, before/after snapshots, and WinGet result remain in the live consolidated report until a new FIX + OPTIMIZE ALL run begins.

sections.heading: Smarter Windows crash classification
sections.detail: Repeated sppsvc.exe crashes are now identified as Windows Software Protection / licensing-component stability evidence instead of being mislabeled as an ordinary third-party app that should be repaired from a vendor. PulseGuard does not perform aggressive licensing/token resets automatically.

sections.heading: Store, Defender, and update-channel reporting
sections.detail: Microsoft Store package-state issues now name the affected package and are review/info findings rather than score-penalizing active warnings. Defender Tamper Protection off is surfaced as informational without force-changing policy, never/no-recorded full-scan sentinel values are normalized, and Windows software updates, Windows driver updates, and WinGet application updates are reported as separate channels.
